descriptionChirho: Conditional conjunction הֵן introducing a protasis ('if') in conditional clauses, sometimes preceded by the conjunction waw ('and if'). This is the standard conditional use, marking a supposition or hypothesis. Translated as English 'if/and if,' Spanish 'si/y si,' Hindi 'yadi' (यदि), Arabic 'in/wa-in' (إِنْ/وَإِنْ), Korean 'manyak' (만약), Swahili 'kama/na kama.' Occurs 12 times in the Hebrew Bible, functioning identically whether or not preceded by waw.

Disjunctive use of הֵן meaning 'or, whether,' introducing an alternative or indirect question rather than a simple conditional. This sense presents options or possibilities rather than hypothetical conditions. Translated as English 'or/whether,' Spanish 'sea,' Hindi 'ya' (या), Arabic 'wa-imma' (وَإِمَّا), Korean 'manyak' (만약), Swahili 'iwe.' Semantically distinct from the conditional 'if' sense in that it marks disjunction between alternatives rather than conditional protasis. Found in 3 occurrences.
